title: Pullback isomorphisms on cohomology: from prime-torsion to torsion sheaves
statement:
Let $u:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with $X$ and $Y$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For an abelian sheaf $G$ on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] let
$$u^*:H^q(X_{\Et},G)\longrightarrow H^q(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}G)\qquad(q\ge0)$$
be the pullback map of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] between the etale cohomology groups of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], $u^{-1}$ the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Assume that for every prime number $r$ and every abelian sheaf $G$ on $X_{\Et}$ with $rG=0$ (i.e. multiplication by $r$ is the zero endomorphism of $G$), $u^*$ is bijective for every $q\ge0$. Then $u^*:H^q(X_{\Et},F)\to H^q(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}F)$ is bijective for every $q\ge0$ and every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf].

proof.text: *Functoriality of $H^q$ and naturality of $u^*$.* For a scheme $T$ and a morphism $\varphi:G\to G'$ of abelian sheaves on $T_{\Et}$, $H^q(\varphi):H^q(T_{\Et},G)\to H^q(T_{\Et},G')$ is defined in the statement of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] from any lift $\tilde\varphi:I^\bullet\to I'^\bullet$ of $\varphi$ to K-injective resolutions $s:G\to I^\bullet$, $s':G'\to I'^\bullet$, and does not depend on the lift. Hence $\varphi\mapsto H^q(\varphi)$ is a functor: $\mathrm{id}$ is a lift of $\mathrm{id}_G$, so $H^q(\mathrm{id}_G)=\mathrm{id}$; if $\tilde\varphi$ lifts $\varphi$ and $\tilde\psi$ lifts $\psi:G'\to G''$ (resolution $s''$), then $\tilde\psi\tilde\varphi s\simeq\tilde\psi s'\varphi\simeq s''\psi\varphi$, so $\tilde\psi\tilde\varphi$ lifts $\psi\varphi$ and $H^q(\psi\varphi)=H^q(\psi)H^q(\varphi)$. In particular $H^q(\varphi)$ is bijective when $\varphi$ is an isomorphism (with inverse $H^q(\varphi^{-1})$). Clause 3 of the same lemma gives, for every morphism $\varphi:G\to G'$ of abelian sheaves on $X_{\Et}$, $u^*\circ H^q(\varphi)=H^q(u^{-1}\varphi)\circ u^*$ (naturality of $u^*$ in the sheaf).

proof.text: *A torsion sheaf is the colimit of its $n$-torsion subsheaves.* Let $F$ be a torsion abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf]. Let $N$ be the set of positive integers ordered by divisibility, a directed poset, hence a filtered small category; for $n\in N$ let $F[n]=\ker(n:F\to F)$ [def-pur-abelian-sheaf-kernel], with the inclusions $j_{nm}:F[n]\subseteq F[m]$ for $n\mid m$ and $j_n:F[n]\subseteq F$. Let $(L,(\iota_n)_n)$ be the colimit of $n\mapsto F[n]$ in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; the canonical map $c_F:L\to F$, characterized by $c_F\circ\iota_n=j_n$, is an isomorphism: this is the definition of a torsion sheaf in [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf]. Moreover $n\cdot F[n]=0$ for every $n$, since $F[n]$ is the kernel of $n$. (Stacks writes this as $\mathcal F=\colim\mathcal F[n]$. The imported [lemma-weil-pbc-torsion-filtered-union] proves the same for the other definition of torsion, "every local section is locally killed by a positive integer"; it is not needed here, since the statement uses [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf], where it is the definition.)

source.place: proof of Lemma 0A4B (lemma-proper-base-change-in-terms-of-injectives), second paragraph: "Then $\mathcal F=\colim\mathcal F[n]$"

proof.text: *Sheaves killed by a positive integer.* Claim: for every integer $n\ge1$ and every abelian sheaf $G$ on $X_{\Et}$ with $nG=0$ (multiplication by $n$ is the zero endomorphism), $u^*:H^q(X_{\Et},G)\to H^q(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}G)$ is bijective for every $q\ge0$. Induction on the number $\Omega(n)$ of prime factors of $n$ counted with multiplicity. If $\Omega(n)=0$, then $n=1$, $G=0$, so $2G=0$ and the hypothesis of the lemma (with $r=2$) applies. If $\Omega(n)=1$, $n$ is a prime and the hypothesis applies. Let $\Omega(n)\ge2$, choose a prime $r\mid n$ and put $m=n/r$, so $\Omega(m)=\Omega(n)-1\ge1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-factor-devissage] (for $n>1$, $r\mid n$, $G$ killed by $n$) there is a short exact sequence $0\to G_1\xrightarrow{\alpha}G\xrightarrow{\beta}G_2\to0$ in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$, with $G_1=G[r]=\ker(r)$, $G_2=rG$ the image of $r:G\to G$ (isomorphic to Stacks' $G/G[r]$), $\beta$ the corestriction of $r$, $rG_1=0$ and $mG_2=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder]: (1) $0\to u^{-1}G_1\to u^{-1}G\to u^{-1}G_2\to0$ is exact on $Y_{\Et}$ (the ladder lemma derives this from the exactness of $u^{-1}$); (2) both sequences have long exact cohomology sequences with connecting maps $\delta^q_X,\delta^q_Y$; (3) the maps $u^*$ commute with $H^q(\alpha),H^q(\beta)$ and the $\delta^q$. Fix $q\ge0$. In the category of abelian groups consider the commutative diagram whose top row is $H^{q-1}(X,G_2)\xrightarrow{\delta^{q-1}_X}H^q(X,G_1)\xrightarrow{H^q(\alpha)}H^q(X,G)\xrightarrow{H^q(\beta)}H^q(X,G_2)\xrightarrow{\delta^q_X}H^{q+1}(X,G_1)$, whose bottom row is the same on $Y$ for the sheaves $u^{-1}G_1,u^{-1}G,u^{-1}G_2$, and whose five vertical maps are the maps $u^*$; for $q=0$ the first entry of each row is replaced by $0$ (and the first vertical map by $0\to0$), which keeps the rows exact because the long exact sequences begin with $0\to H^0(G_1)$. The squares commute by (3) (the first one trivially when $q=0$), and the rows are exact at the three middle places by (2). The four outer vertical maps are bijective: $u^*$ on $H^{q-1}(G_2)$ and $H^q(G_2)$ by the induction hypothesis for $G_2$ ($mG_2=0$, $\Omega(m)<\Omega(n)$), $u^*$ on $H^q(G_1)$ and $H^{q+1}(G_1)$ by the hypothesis of the lemma for $G_1$ ($rG_1=0$). This uses the induction hypothesis and the hypothesis of the lemma in the degrees $q-1$, $q$, $q+1$ at once, which is why both are stated for all $q$. Bijective homomorphisms are the isomorphisms of the abelian category of abelian groups, so the five lemma [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] (Mathlib, in this form for groups: AddMonoidHom.bijective_of_surjective_of_bijective_of_bijective_of_injective) shows that $u^*:H^q(X_{\Et},G)\to H^q(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}G)$ is bijective. This completes the induction. (The same induction, for another property stable under extensions, is lemma-weil-pbc-prime-factor-induction of unit sk-thm-iff, and in Lean CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.prop_of_nsmul_id_eq_zero; it is written out here.)

proof.text: *Passage to the colimit.* Let $F$ be torsion, with $L,\iota_n,j_n,j_{nm},c_F$ as in Step 2; fix $q\ge0$. By Step 3 (each $F[n]$ is killed by $n$) the maps $u^*_n:H^q(X,F[n])\to H^q(Y,u^{-1}F[n])$ are bijective. (a) On $X$: $n\mapsto H^q(X,F[n])$, with transition maps $H^q(j_{nm})$, is a directed system of abelian groups (Step 1), with colimit $\varinjlim_nH^q(X,F[n])$ and coprojections $\lambda_n$ [def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups]; the maps $H^q(\iota_n)$ are compatible (Step 1: $\iota_m j_{nm}=\iota_n$), and the induced canonical map $\kappa_X:\varinjlim_nH^q(X,F[n])\to H^q(X,L)$, $\kappa_X\lambda_n=H^q(\iota_n)$, is bijective by [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-filtered-colimit], $X$ being quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. (b) On $Y$: let $(L',(\iota'_n))$ be the colimit of $n\mapsto u^{-1}F[n]$ (transition maps $u^{-1}j_{nm}$); the canonical map $\theta:L'\to u^{-1}L$, $\theta\iota'_n=u^{-1}\iota_n$, is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-preserves-colimits], and $\kappa_Y:\varinjlim_nH^q(Y,u^{-1}F[n])\to H^q(Y,L')$, $\kappa_Y\lambda'_n=H^q(\iota'_n)$, is bijective by [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-filtered-colimit], $Y$ being quasi-compact and quasi-separated. (c) By naturality (Step 1) $u^*_mH^q(j_{nm})=H^q(u^{-1}j_{nm})u^*_n$, so the $u^*_n$ form a morphism of directed systems and induce $\mu=\varinjlim u^*_n$ with $\mu\lambda_n=\lambda'_nu^*_n$; since each $u^*_n$ is bijective, the inverses $(u^*_n)^{-1}$ also form a morphism of directed systems, and the map they induce is inverse to $\mu$ by the uniqueness in the universal property, so $\mu$ is bijective. (d) For every $n$, using Step 1, $H^q(\theta)\kappa_Y\mu\lambda_n=H^q(\theta)H^q(\iota'_n)u^*_n=H^q(u^{-1}\iota_n)u^*_n=u^*_LH^q(\iota_n)=u^*_L\kappa_X\lambda_n$, where $u^*_L:H^q(X,L)\to H^q(Y,u^{-1}L)$; by the uniqueness in the universal property of $\varinjlim_nH^q(X,F[n])$, $u^*_L\kappa_X=H^q(\theta)\kappa_Y\mu$. The right side is a composite of bijections ($H^q(\theta)$ by Step 1, $\theta$ being an isomorphism) and $\kappa_X$ is bijective, so $u^*_L$ is bijective. (e) Finally naturality for the isomorphism $c_F:L\to F$ gives $u^*_F\circ H^q(c_F)=H^q(u^{-1}c_F)\circ u^*_L$, with $H^q(c_F)$ and $H^q(u^{-1}c_F)$ bijective (Step 1), so $u^*_F:H^q(X_{\Et},F)\to H^q(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}F)$ is bijective. As $q\ge0$ was arbitrary, this proves the lemma.
